title: Product of Array Except Self
statement: You are given a list of integers nums with length at least 2. The list may contain zeros and negative numbers. Build and return a new list answer of the same length where answer[i] equals the product of every element of nums other than nums[i]. Return the values in the same index order as nums. You must not use division at any point; instead combine a left-to-right running product of everything before index i with a right-to-left running product of everything after index i. Note that when nums contains exactly one zero, every answer entry is 0 except at the zero's own position, and when nums contains two or more zeros every answer entry is 0.
reference_solution:
def products_except_self(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    answer = [1] * n
    prefix = 1
    for i in range(n):
        answer[i] = prefix
        prefix *= nums[i]
    suffix = 1
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        answer[i] *= suffix
        suffix *= nums[i]
    return answer
hints: You cannot divide the total product by each element, so how could two sweeps in opposite directions supply what each position needs?
For index i the answer is (product of everything to its left) times (product of everything to its right); maintain a running prefix product and a running suffix product.

First pass left to right: set answer[i] to the running product of elements before i, then fold nums[i] into that running product. Second pass right to left: multiply answer[i] by a running product of elements after i, then fold nums[i] into it. Zeros fall out naturally with no special casing.
